q: Chemistry is after all the study of all ____, its composition, its properties, and its transformation from one form to another.
e: Chemistry is after all the study of all matter, its composition, its properties, and its transformation from one form to another. Chemistry studies matter and the changes matter undergoes.

q: Nowadays, there is a fourth state known as '____' which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles.
e: Nowadays, there is a fourth state known as 'plasma' which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles. Plasma is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Matter is made up of ____ particles.
e: Matter is made up of tiny particles. Tiny is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These can be atoms or ____ (groups of atoms), and elements or compounds.
e: These can be atoms or molecules (groups of atoms), and elements or compounds. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The air (gas), the sea water (liquid), and alloys (solid) are not pure substances; they are ____.
e: The air (gas), the sea water (liquid), and alloys (solid) are not pure substances; they are mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: Different methods of separation depend on whether the substances to be separated are solids, liquids or ____.
e: Different methods of separation depend on whether the substances to be separated are solids, liquids or gases. Gases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The most common states of matter are solid, liquid and ____.
e: The most common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas. Gas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The properties of each state of matter depend on the forces of attraction between the particles which can be weak or ____.
e: The properties of each state of matter depend on the forces of attraction between the particles which can be weak or strong. Strong is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one ____.
e: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one another. Another is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solids have a definite shape and ____.
e: Solids have a definite shape and volume. Volume is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Liquids are composed of particles which are not fixed in any definite positions as in the ____.
e: Liquids are composed of particles which are not fixed in any definite positions as in the solids. In a solid, particles are packed tightly with strong forces, so the shape is fixed.

q: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in ____.
e: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in gases. Gases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between ____ particles.
e: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between gaseous particles. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hence, gases do not have a definite volume and shape of their ____.
e: Hence, gases do not have a definite volume and shape of their own. Own is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It can be clearly visible in particles of smoke suspended in a gas because of the effect known as ____ motion.
e: It can be clearly visible in particles of smoke suspended in a gas because of the effect known as Brownian motion. Brownian motion is the random jiggling of tiny particles hit by fast molecules in a fluid.

q: Diffusion can be explained by the ____ motion.
e: Diffusion can be explained by the Brownian motion. Brownian motion is the random jiggling of tiny particles hit by fast molecules in a fluid.

q: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of ____ substance.
e: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of another substance. Another is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and ____.
e: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and gases. Gases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the ____.
e: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles ____.
e: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles diffuse. Diffuse is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse ____.
e: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse faster. Faster is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from collisions with the gas or liquid ____.
e: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from collisions with the gas or liquid particles. In a liquid, particles touch but can slide, so volume is fixed while shape is not. In a gas, particles are far apart, move fast, and have weak attractions.

q: One way to classify properties is based on whether or not chemical composition of an object is changed by the act of observing the ____.
e: One way to classify properties is based on whether or not chemical composition of an object is changed by the act of observing the property. A property is physical if measuring it leaves the substance itself unchanged, and chemical if composition changes. A chemical property describes how a substance reacts to make something new.

q: Changes in substances can be classified as either physical or ____.
e: Changes in substances can be classified as either physical or chemical. A chemical change makes new substances, like burning or cooking rice.

q: A physical change is a change in which no new substances are ____.
e: A physical change is a change in which no new substances are formed. If no new substance is formed, the change is physical.

q: Melting, boiling, freezing, evaporation, vaporisation, condensation and sublimation are considered as ____ changes.
e: Melting, boiling, freezing, evaporation, vaporisation, condensation and sublimation are considered as physical changes. A physical change does not make a new substance; melting and boiling are typical examples.

q: The temperature at which a solid melts is called the ____ point.
e: The temperature at which a solid melts is called the melting point. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places.

q: Vaporisation is the process that occurs when a chemical or element is converted from a liquid to a ____.
e: Vaporisation is the process that occurs when a chemical or element is converted from a liquid to a vapour. Vapour is the gas form of a substance that is usually liquid, made by vaporisation.

q: Evaporation is the process of a substance in a liquid state changing to a gaseous state due to an increase in temperature and / or ____.
e: Evaporation is the process of a substance in a liquid state changing to a gaseous state due to an increase in temperature and / or pressure. Raising temperature or lowering pressure helps a liquid evaporate.

q: Boiling is the rapid vaporisation of a liquid, which occurs when a liquid is heated to its ____ point.
e: Boiling is the rapid vaporisation of a liquid, which occurs when a liquid is heated to its boiling point. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

q: For example, iodine solid changes to iodine vapour, where heat is absorbed, and this is known as ____.
e: For example, iodine solid changes to iodine vapour, where heat is absorbed, and this is known as sublimation. Sublimation is solid going straight to gas, or the reverse, without a liquid stage.

q: Water vapour turns to frost is an example of ____.
e: Water vapour turns to frost is an example of deposition. Deposition is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A chemical change is a change in which one or more new substances are ____.
e: A chemical change is a change in which one or more new substances are formed. If no new substance is formed, the change is physical.

q: Chemical changes occur via chemical reactions such as dissociation, neutralisation, ____, etc.
e: Chemical changes occur via chemical reactions such as dissociation, neutralisation, precipitation, etc. Precipitation is formation of an insoluble solid from a solution.

q: The temperature at which a solid changes to a liquid state at one atmospheric pressure is called ____ point of that solid.
e: The temperature at which a solid changes to a liquid state at one atmospheric pressure is called melting point of that solid. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places.

q: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the atmospheric pressure of the surrounding is called the ____ point.
e: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid is equal to the atmospheric pressure of the surrounding is called the boiling point. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

q: Condensation is the change from a gaseous state to its ____ state.
e: Condensation is the change from a gaseous state to its liquid state. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Sublimation is the change of solid state directly into gaseous state without ____.
e: Sublimation is the change of solid state directly into gaseous state without melting. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places.

q: Deposition is the direct solidification of a vapour by cooling; the reverse of ____.
e: Deposition is the direct solidification of a vapour by cooling; the reverse of sublimation. Sublimation is solid going straight to gas, or the reverse, without a liquid stage.

q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and ____.
e: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant ____.
e: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant composition. Composition is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pure substances are classified as either elements or ____.
e: Pure substances are classified as either elements or compounds. A compound contains two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. A pure substance has a fixed composition, either an element or a compound.

q: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms, which were invisible and ____.
e: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms, which were invisible and indivisible. Atoms can be split into protons, neutrons, and electrons, so they are not truly indivisible.

q: Today, the atom is still considered as the basic unit of any ____.
e: Today, the atom is still considered as the basic unit of any element. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom, e.g., carbon element is made up of carbon ____.
e: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom, e.g., carbon element is made up of carbon atoms. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Atoms are the smallest particles into which an element can be ____.
e: Atoms are the smallest particles into which an element can be divided. Divided is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined ____.
e: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined state. State is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Substances like these, which cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means, are called ____.
e: Substances like these, which cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means, are called elements. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: On the basis of their properties, elements may be classified into two groups, metals and ____.
e: On the basis of their properties, elements may be classified into two groups, metals and non-metals. Non-metals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Metals show metallic ____.
e: Metals show metallic luster. Luster is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most of the metals are malleable and ____.
e: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile. Ductile is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Metals are good conductors of heat and ____.
e: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Non-metals are usually ____.
e: Non-metals are usually brittle. Brittle is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most of the non-metals are poor conductors of heat and ____.
e: Most of the non-metals are poor conductors of heat and electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The atoms of some elements are joined together in small groups called ____.
e: The atoms of some elements are joined together in small groups called molecules. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A molecule of an element (molecular element) consists of atoms of the ____ kind.
e: A molecule of an element (molecular element) consists of atoms of the same kind. Same is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A molecule of a compound (molecular compound) consists of more than one kind of ____.
e: A molecule of a compound (molecular compound) consists of more than one kind of atoms. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The atoms of different elements in the molecule of a compound are combined in a definite ____.
e: The atoms of different elements in the molecule of a compound are combined in a definite ratio. A compound contains two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio. Here they want ratio.

q: Most substances on earth occur as compounds, e.g. carbon dioxide ($CO_2$), water ($H_2O$), marble ($CaCO_3$), glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$), ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) and ____.
e: Most substances on earth occur as compounds, e.g. carbon dioxide (CO2), water (H2O), marble (CaCO3), glucose (C6H12O6), ethanol (C2H5OH) and ammonia (NH3). Ammonia (NH3) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a ____ molecule.
e: Hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a diatomic molecule. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Water is formed by combining two different elements: H and O, so it is a ____ molecule (binary compound).
e: Water is formed by combining two different elements: H and O, so it is a triatomic molecule (binary compound). Triatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In ammonia, there are more than three atoms from two different elements: N and H, so it is a ____ molecule (binary compound).
e: In ammonia, there are more than three atoms from two different elements: N and H, so it is a polyatomic molecule (binary compound). Polyatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In ethanol, there are more than three atoms from three different elements, so it is a polyatomic molecule (____ compound).
e: In ethanol, there are more than three atoms from three different elements, so it is a polyatomic molecule (ternary compound). Ternary is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not ____ combined.
e: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not chemically combined. Chemically is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They do not have well defined specific properties and the substances are not in fixed ____.
e: They do not have well defined specific properties and the substances are not in fixed ratios. Ratios is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mixtures may also be heterogeneous or ____.
e: The mixtures may also be heterogeneous or homogeneous. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution.

q: Therefore, the mixtures can be classified as two main categories: homogeneous and ____ mixtures.
e: Therefore, the mixtures can be classified as two main categories: homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts.

q: Apart from alloys containing two metals, solid-solid mixtures are ____.
e: Apart from alloys containing two metals, solid-solid mixtures are heterogeneous. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts.

q: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a ____.
e: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid ____ state.
e: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid crystalline state. Crystalline is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Decantation is a process to separate ____.
e: Decantation is a process to separate mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is ____ in nature.
e: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is magnetic in nature. Magnetic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be ____.
e: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be separated. Separated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a ____ column.
e: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a fractionating column. A fractionating column lets a liquid mixture split into fractions with different boiling points.

q: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and ____ speed.
e: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and rotor speed. Rotor is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chromatography is a separation method of the mixed substances that depends on the speed at which they move through special media, or chemical ____.
e: Chromatography is a separation method of the mixed substances that depends on the speed at which they move through special media, or chemical substances. Substances is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a solid) and a mobile phase (a liquid or a ____).
e: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a solid) and a mobile phase (a liquid or a gas). Gas is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A solution is a homogeneous (uniform) mixture of two or more ____.
e: A solution is a homogeneous (uniform) mixture of two or more substances. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary.

q: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's ____.
e: The ocean is a vast water solution containing different compounds extracted from the minerals of the Earth's crust. Crust is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Sugar is the solute, and water is the ____.
e: Sugar is the solute, and water is the solvent. The solvent is the liquid that does the dissolving, often water.

q: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions (____ liquids), while some liquids do not mix (immiscible liquids).
e: Some liquids can mix with one another in all proportions (miscible liquids), while some liquids do not mix (immiscible liquids). Miscible is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solutions may be gaseous, solid, or ____ in nature.
e: Solutions may be gaseous, solid, or liquid in nature. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Dry air is a familiar example of a ____ solution.
e: Dry air is a familiar example of a gaseous solution. Gaseous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Brass (copper and zinc) is an example of a ____ solution.
e: Brass (copper and zinc) is an example of a solid solution. Solid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as ____ solutions.
e: Solutions having water as the solvent are referred to as aqueous solutions. Aqueous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an ____ solution.
e: If some more solid added can dissolve with stirring, this solution is known as an unsaturated solution. Unsaturated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A ____ solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred.
e: A saturated solution forms when no more solute can be dissolved in the given amount of solvent at that temperature even if it is stirred. Saturated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The amount (in grams) of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the ____ of that solute.
e: The amount (in grams) of the solute in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution at that experimental temperature is known as the solubility of that solute. Solubility is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a ____ solution.
e: If the solution contains more solute than it should have at room temperature, it is a supersaturated solution. Supersaturated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Solubility of the solute depends, in part, on the temperature of the ____.
e: Solubility of the solute depends, in part, on the temperature of the solvent. The solvent is the liquid that does the dissolving, often water.

q: When the temperature of the solution is increased the solubility of the solute ____.
e: When the temperature of the solution is increased the solubility of the solute increases. Increases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: There are some exceptions, such as the solubility of all gases and some solids like calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate, which decreases when temperature of the solution is ____.
e: There are some exceptions, such as the solubility of all gases and some solids like calcium hydroxide and calcium sulphate, which decreases when temperature of the solution is increased. Increased is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility ____.
e: When a saturated solution at a higher temperature is cooled, the solubility decreases. Decreases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A solute is a substance which dissolves in a solvent to give a ____.
e: A solute is a substance which dissolves in a solvent to give a solution. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute dissolved in solvent.

q: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a ____ mixture.
e: A solvent is a substance, mostly liquid, in which another substance dissolves to give a homogeneous mixture. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution.

q: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate ____ g of water, at that temperature.
e: Solubility of a substance at a given temperature is the mass in grams of the substance which will saturate 100 g of water, at that temperature. 100 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Matter is everything that we come across in our lives, like the air you breathe, the clothes you wear and the water you ____.
e: Matter is everything that we come across in our lives, like the air you breathe, the clothes you wear and the water you drink. Drink is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through ____ means.
e: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through chemical means. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed ____.
e: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed ratio. Ratio is the idea that completes this fact.
